body:
Independent fresh-context reviews of the exact head `033ea871a22f40b872837cbf397f2d9c1c84b007`, by two models of different families, each in a fresh read-only context that did not author the change.

**Both verdicts: APPROVE WITH NITS — no P0 findings, no P1 findings.**

The reviews drove two rounds of fixes, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-change code:

- The limit did not reach a request that declares no length: the framework cuts such a body short without a word, so the excess went unnoticed and the request was answered from the truncated text. The body is now read from the raw input with a limit of its own.
- The server in front of the application refused a body of exactly the limit and answered with plain text, so the application never saw the request and the answer had no OpenAI shape. The server now has a limit a little larger than the application's, so the application refuses the body and the answer carries the OpenAI shape.
- An image of one byte over the limit shares its encoded length with one exactly at the limit, so the size was only known after the decode. The bound now covers every encoded length a payload within the limit can have, and the changelog says that only a payload far over the limit is refused before it is decoded.
- The two things that actually stop a body from being read into memory — the length the body is read with, and the refusal of a body that declares a length over the limit — were not held by any test; removing either left the suite green. Each now has a test, and a body of exactly the limit is accepted.

What the reviews verified: the largest body accepted is the same for a declared length, an undeclared length and a chunked request; the base64 arithmetic never rejects a payload that decodes within the limit; a legitimate 10 MB inline image still fits; and the connection stays usable after both kinds of refusal.

The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on this head.
